slides.title:
"Why are you
leaving academia?"
slides.body: Almost every PhD hears it. Here's how to answer.
slides.say: Why are you leaving academia? Almost every P H D hears this in industry interviews. Here's how to answer it.

slides.title:
Toward this job, or
away from academia?
slides.body: They want to know you'll thrive with deadlines, teams and goals.
slides.say: The interviewer wants to know one thing. Are you running toward this job, or just away from academia? And will you thrive with deadlines and teams?

slides.title:
Talk about the pull,
not the push.
slides.before: Funding is awful and there are no jobs.
slides.after: I want my work used by real customers.
slides.say: Tip one. Talk about the pull, not the push. Not, funding is awful and there are no jobs. Instead, I want my work used by real customers.

slides.title: Back it with one real example.
slides.body: A collaboration, an internship, or a project with industry partners.
slides.say: Tip two. Back it up with one real example, like a collaboration or internship that showed you this path fits.

slides.title: Keep it short. Then pivot.
slides.body: Thirty seconds, then link it to this role.
slides.say: Tip three. Keep it to about thirty seconds, then connect it to why you want this role.
